# Peru at the FIFA World Cup

Peru participated in the World Cup during the first [World Cup in 1930](/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup "1930 FIFA World Cup") and has participated in [qualifiers](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "FIFA World Cup qualification") since 1958.

Peru were invited to the first [FIFA World Cup](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") in Uruguay in 1930. They lost both of their games and finished 10th out of 13 teams. The team either withdrew or did not enter the next four tournaments, in 1934, 1938, 1950, and 1954. Peru participated but did not [qualify](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "FIFA World Cup qualification") in 1958, 1962, or 1966.

Peru had its best result in [Mexico 1970](/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup"), finishing in seventh place. Peru again finished in the top eight at the World Cup in [Argentina 1978](/wiki/1978_FIFA_World_Cup "1978 FIFA World Cup"). They finished first in their group during the first round of the tournament, but were eliminated after losing all their games in the second round. Peru reached the next World Cup finals in [Spain 1982](/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"), although the team was eliminated in the first round after 2 draws and 1 loss. From 1986 to 2014, Peru did not advance past the [CONMEBOL](/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") qualifying round.

After finishing fifth in [CONMEBOL qualifying](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(CONMEBOL) "2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)"), Peru reached the [2018 finals](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup") by defeating New Zealand in an [intercontinental play-off](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(OFC%E2%80%93CONMEBOL_play-off) "2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (OFC–CONMEBOL play-off)"). title: Who Will Win the 2026 FIFA World Cup? The Opta Supercomputer ...
content:
We asked the supercomputer to simulate the 2026 World Cup 25,000 times, and it has produced some fascinating conclusions in its official pre-tournament predictions.

## World Cup 2026 Predictions

   Spain are the most likely winners of the 2026 World Cup, winning the tournament in 16.1% of the 25,000 pre-tournament simulations by the Opta supercomputer.
   France, England and Argentina follow close behind, all winning the World Cup in more than 10% of the simulations.
   Co-hosts United States, Mexico and Canada are very unlikely to win the World Cup based on the supercomputer sims.
   Just 35.9% of the 25,000 Opta supercomputer simulations saw a nation win the World Cup for the first time ever.

## Spain are the World Cup Favourites [...] # Who Will Win the 2026 FIFA World Cup? The Opta Supercomputer Predictions | Opta Analyst
 more goals than ever before.

Teams will battle it out to emerge from 12 different groups and reach a knockout stage that now features a round of 32 – a new addition at international football’s showpiece event.

It is Argentina who go into the World Cup as defending champions after Lionel Messi helped to guide _La Albiceleste_ to a famous triumph in Qatar towards the end of 2022.

They are one of six participants from South America, along with five-time winners Brazil, who are now led by Carlo Ancelotti as the Seleção seek to end a barren run since claiming their last crown back in 2002. [...] In a five-week knockout competition there is massive variance. Just one shock exit from a tournament favourite can cause other dominos to fall and the draw can suddenly open up for an unexpected team to challenge.

With that in mind, there are not many outcomes which can be completely dismissed. But there is one scenario our supercomputer _is_ willing to rule out, as the only team who never won the tournament in any of our 25,000 simulations was Curaçao.So, yes, Haiti unbelievably won the 2026 World Cup once in our 25,000 simulations.

## Winner

Burke: As much as I’d love to say England, France are surely favourites. Results rarely go as predicted, but if France win their group, they might not face a side on a similar level until a potential semi-final against Spain. [...] Carlo Ancelotti’s side will get better, stronger and more confident with each passing match. It will start with a commanding win against Morocco on Saturday. While many people expect Brazil to underachieve, I believe they will find their form in the same setting that saw them lift the 1994 World Cup trophy.

Lang:Ecuador were the story of South American qualifying, finishing second behind Argentina (and ahead of Brazil, Colombia and Uruguay) despite a three-point deduction for a rules violation in the previous World Cup cycle.

Their success was almost entirely down to their defensive solidity — they remarkably conceded just five times across their 18 matches. They won’t win many awards for aesthetics, but they’ll take some beating. [...] Advertisement

Anka: It’s not an exact science, but Golden Boot winners are typically strikers who take the penalties on teams that reach at least the quarter-finals. They tend to score most of their goals in the group stage, putting the weaker sides to the sword, before perhaps picking up an assist or two in the knockout games to help with a tiebreaker.
